_readme: All thresholds, comparators, source links, dates and interface copy live in this file. When the LGC changes a threshold or Kara changes wording, edit only this file. Placeholders in {braces} are filled in by script.js. Each indicator states the comparison that CREATES an FPIC (the guide states thresholds in the avoid-an-FPIC direction). Indicator types: bandedPercent, percentOfBase, value, yesNo.
draftNotice: Draft for testing. Thresholds and wording are waiting for final review by Kara Millonzi.

article.text: Understanding and Using the LGC's Financial Performance Indicators (Coates' Canons)

copy.title: FPIC Calculator
copy.purpose: Check your unit against the 17 indicators the Local Government Commission (LGC) uses to decide whether a unit gets a Financial Performance Indicator of Concern (FPIC). Enter only what you have from your audit and skip the rest.
copy.privacy: Your numbers stay in your browser.
copy.noscript: This calculator needs JavaScript. Your numbers never leave your browser.
copy.unitTypeHelp: The LGC uses different thresholds for municipalities and counties. This affects indicator 1 only.
copy.unitNameHelp: Shown on the printed summary only.
copy.errExpendituresPositive: General Fund expenditures must be greater than $0.
copy.errYearIncomplete: Enter both amounts for this year, or leave both blank.
copy.messageAbove: Your General Fund is {points} above the level that would create an FPIC, a cushion of {dollars}.
copy.messageAt: Your General Fund is exactly at the threshold. A result at or above the threshold does not create an FPIC, but there is no cushion.
copy.messageBelow: This result would create an FPIC. It is {dollars} below the threshold ({points}). An FPIC requires a response from your governing board; it does not by itself mean financial distress.
copy.responseNote: The board's written response is due to the LGC within {days} days after the auditor presents the audit (20 NCAC 03 .0508).
copy.barLabel: Where you are compared with the threshold
copy.aboutThreshold: The LGC uses {pct}% as the point where a response is required for a {noun} with General Fund expenditures of {band}. It is not a recommended target, and the LGC has said there is no state or LGC minimum for fund balance.
copy.askFpic: Before you respond, ask two questions. Was this change planned, such as saving for a specific purchase? Is it one-time or recurring? A one-time use of reserves and a recurring gap between revenues and spending can produce the same number, but they call for different responses.
copy.whatIfIntro: Enter the fund balance your budget plans to appropriate. The scenario subtracts it from fund balance available and from total fund balance, and keeps expenditures the same.
copy.appropriationHelp: In dollars. Leave blank to skip.
copy.whatIfEmpty: Enter a planned appropriation to compare.
copy.whatIfNeedResult: Complete the numbers above to run the what-if.
copy.whatIfCross: This appropriation would move your result from no FPIC to an FPIC, from a cushion of {before} to a shortfall of {after}.
copy.whatIfShrink: This appropriation leaves the result above the threshold. The cushion would shrink from {before} to {after}.
copy.whatIfGrow: The result is already below the threshold. This appropriation would grow the shortfall from {before} to {after}.
copy.whatIfOverdraw: The appropriation is larger than fund balance available, so the scenario shows a negative balance.
copy.whatIfCaveat: This is a simple estimate. It assumes nothing else changes during the year. It does not predict your year-end results, and the LGC calculates fund balance available from audited statements.
copy.trendIntro: Add up to three prior years. The current year comes from your numbers above.
copy.trendCurrentNote: Uses the numbers you entered above.
copy.trendNeedMore: Add at least one prior year to see a chart and trend note.
copy.trendNeedResult: Choose a unit type and complete your numbers above to see the trend.
copy.chartSummary: Line chart of fund balance available as a percent of General Fund expenditures. {points}. The data table follows.
copy.driftAbove: Fund balance available has fallen {n} years in a row, from {from} ({fromYear}) to {to} ({toYear}). It is still above the threshold, but the direction is worth a look.
copy.driftBelow: Fund balance available has fallen {n} years in a row, from {from} ({fromYear}) to {to} ({toYear}), and the current result is below the threshold.
copy.printHeading: Summary for your board or manager
copy.footerSource: Thresholds: {guideLink}, Tables 1 to 3. Thresholds as of {asOf}, checked against the guide on {checked}. The LGC may change its thresholds, so check the {lgcLink} for the current guide. See also {articleLink}.
copy.footerDisclaimer: Educational tool, not an LGC determination. An FPIC is a flag for attention, not a finding of financial distress, and this tool cannot verify your yes or no answers.
copy.eyebrow: NC Finance Connect | UNC School of Government
copy.errTooLarge: That number is too large. Enter whole dollars, such as 20,000,000.
copy.promptUnit: Choose a unit type to see a result.
copy.summaryNone: No FPICs on the {checked} indicators you checked.
copy.summaryNoneOne: No FPIC on the 1 indicator you checked.
copy.summaryEmpty: Nothing checked yet. Enter what you have; skip the rest.
copy.nextLgcLink: Read the LGC page on FPIs and responses
copy.whatIfRow2Cross: The appropriation would also create an FPIC on indicator 2, appropriated fund balance, because total fund balance would fall from the prior year-end.
copy.whatIfRow3Cross: The appropriation would also create an FPIC on indicator 3, because total fund balance would be 0 or less.
copy.printAsOf: Thresholds as of {asOf}. Educational tool, not an LGC determination.
copy.step2Intro: Open a section and fill in the rows you can. Results update as you type. A row you leave blank is not checked.
copy.exampleBanner: You are looking at example numbers, not yours.
copy.panelEmpty: Enter a number in any row to see a result. You can skip rows you do not have.
copy.headlineNone: No FPIC on the {checked} indicators you entered
copy.headlineNoneOne: No FPIC on the 1 indicator you entered
copy.panelNote: Your yes and no answers are your own. This tool cannot verify them, and it checks only the rows you fill in.
copy.waterQuestion: Does your unit run a water or sewer fund?
copy.waterNaNote: Indicators 4 to 8 will be marked not applicable and left out of your results.
copy.goFurtherIntro: Two extra tools that use your General Fund numbers.
copy.whatIfCardText: See what a planned use of fund balance would do to indicators 1 to 3.
copy.trendCardText: Compare up to four years of fund balance available, with a chart and a note if it keeps falling.
copy.nextHeadingQuiet: What happens if an indicator creates an FPIC?

terms.def: Local Government Commission, the state body that reviews every unit’s annual audit.
Financial Performance Indicator. A number from your audited statements with a threshold attached.
Financial Performance Indicator of Concern. An indicator outside its threshold. Your governing board must send the LGC a written response.
The part of the General Fund’s reserves that is available to spend. Enter it from your audit; the tool does not calculate it.
Dollars above (cushion) or below (shortfall) the point where an indicator would create an FPIC.

groups.label: General Fund
groups.intro: Your main operating fund. Indicators 1 to 3.

groups.label: Water and sewer fund
groups.summary: Only if your unit has a water or sewer fund
groups.intro: Only if your unit runs a water or sewer fund. Indicators 4 to 8.

groups.label: Other checks
groups.intro: Property taxes, audit results and legal requirements. Indicators 9 to 17.

exp.label: General Fund expenditures
exp.help: Use the same expenditures figure the LGC uses in your audit.

fba.label: Fund balance available
fba.help: Enter fund balance available from your audit. The tool does not calculate it.

priorFb.label: Total fund balance at the end of the prior year
priorFb.help: We compare it with this year's total fund balance (row 3).

totalFb.label: General Fund total fund balance at year-end

fba.label: Fund balance available (FBA) as a percentage of expenditures
fba.display: Fund balance available as a percent of expenditures: {value}
fba.fpicWhen: Fund balance available is below the threshold percentage of General Fund expenditures for your unit type and size
fba.why: FBA is the part of your reserves you can appropriate. It gives you cash flow, a cushion for emergencies and unexpected costs, and room when revenues decline. The LGC sets a threshold by unit size. It is the point where a response is required, not a recommended level.

apprFb.label: Appropriated fund balance (change in fund balance)
apprFb.plainLabel: Did total fund balance grow this year?
apprFb.exactlyMsg: No change in total fund balance would create an FPIC. The change must be positive.
apprFb.fpicWhen: Total fund balance did not grow from the prior year-end (a change of 0 or less)
apprFb.why: Appropriating fund balance to cover operating losses can point to an ongoing gap. If the pattern continues, your available reserves decline.

totalFb.label: Total fund balance
totalFb.plainLabel: Is total General Fund balance above zero?
totalFb.exactlyMsg: A total fund balance of exactly $0 would create an FPIC. It must be positive.
totalFb.fpicWhen: Total fund balance is 0 or less
totalFb.why: A deficit means your revenues and other receipts have not been enough to support operations.

cari.label: Capital assets condition ratio
cari.plainLabel: Condition of water and sewer assets
cari.help: The ratio from your water and sewer statements, for example 0.62.
cari.exactlyMsg: A ratio of exactly 0.50 does not create an FPIC.
cari.why: The ratio estimates how much useful life your assets have left. A value below 0.50 can mean assets will need replacing soon.

oni.label: Operating net income, excluding depreciation, including debt service principal and interest
oni.plainLabel: Does the utility cover its costs and debt?
oni.help: Leave out depreciation. Include debt principal and interest. May be negative.
oni.exactlyMsg: Operating net income of exactly $0 would create an FPIC. It must be greater than zero.
oni.fpicWhen: Operating net income is 0 or less
oni.why: A zero or negative amount means your rates are not covering operating costs and debt service.

quick.label: Quick ratio
quick.plainLabel: Can the utility pay short-term bills?
quick.help: Read both from the fund's statement of net position.
quick.exactlyMsg: A quick ratio of exactly 1 does not create an FPIC.
quick.fpicWhen: Current assets divided by current liabilities is below 1
quick.why: The quick ratio measures liquidity. Below 1 means current liabilities exceed unrestricted cash and investments plus accounts receivable, and the fund may struggle to meet expenses. If that continues, the fund may not be sustainable.

transfers.label: Transfers-in to support operations
transfers.plainLabel: Reliance on transfers from other funds
transfers.help: Transfers from other funds that support operations.
transfers.display: Transfers-in as a percent of operating expenses: {value}
transfers.exactlyMsg: Transfers-in of exactly 3% of operating expenses would create an FPIC.
transfers.fpicWhen: Transfers-in are 3% or more of the fund’s operating expenses
transfers.why: Water and sewer rates should cover the fund's operating expenses without operating subsidies or transfers from other funds.

cashPct.label: Unrestricted cash to total expenses ratio
cashPct.help: Include debt principal and interest in expenses. Leave out depreciation.
cashPct.display: Unrestricted cash as a percent of total expenses: {value}
cashPct.exactlyMsg: Unrestricted cash of exactly 16% would create an FPIC.
cashPct.fpicWhen: Unrestricted cash is 16% or less of total expenses
cashPct.why: This shows how many months of expenses your unrestricted cash covers at year-end. 16% is roughly two months.

audit.label: Date audited financial statements were submitted to the LGC
audit.plainLabel: Was the audit submitted on time?
audit.question: Did you submit your audit to the LGC by December 31?
audit.fpicWhen: You did not submit the audit by December 31
audit.why: The governing body is responsible for making the annual audit available to the public on time.
audit.help: The guide sets December 31 for units with a June 30 year-end. If your year-end differs, skip this row.

taxes.label: Amount of budgeted ad valorem tax (including motor vehicles) uncollected
taxes.display: Uncollected taxes as a percent of budgeted taxes: {value}
taxes.exactlyMsg: Uncollected taxes of exactly 3% of the budgeted amount would create an FPIC.
taxes.fpicWhen: Uncollected taxes are 3% or more of budgeted ad valorem taxes
taxes.why: Uncollected taxes above 3% of the budgeted amount can point to negative economic events, inaccurate budgeting or collection problems.

reval.label: Expected change in property value at next revaluation
reval.plainLabel: Do you expect values to fall at revaluation?
reval.question: Do you expect property values to decrease at your next revaluation?
reval.fpicWhen: You expect property values to decrease at the next revaluation
reval.why: A decrease in property value could mean lost tax revenue.
reval.help: This looks ahead, not at the audited year.

budget.label: Budget violations at the adopted ordinance level
budget.plainLabel: Did spending exceed the adopted budget?
budget.question: Did any expenditure go over the adopted budget ordinance?
budget.fpicWhen: An expenditure went over the adopted budget ordinance
budget.why: Spending over the ordinance may mean your purchase order, contract approval or payment process does not comply with G.S. Chapter 159.
budget.help: Overexpenditures at the level your ordinance sets.

findings.label: Material weaknesses, significant deficiencies, statutory violations and/or other audit finding items identified to be addressed in the FPIC response
findings.shortLabel: Audit findings to address in the response
findings.question: Did the auditor report a material weakness, significant deficiency or statutory violation, or another finding that needs a response?
findings.fpicWhen: The audit reports a material weakness, significant deficiency, statutory violation or other finding that needs a response
findings.why: 20 NCAC 03 .0508 requires a response to each significant deficiency, material weakness and other audit finding. Those responses are presented to the governing body and addressed in your FPIC response.
findings.help: Check the findings in your audit report.

foAppointed.label: A finance officer or interim finance officer was appointed for the entire fiscal year
foAppointed.plainLabel: Finance officer in place all year?
foAppointed.question: Did you have a finance officer or interim finance officer for the entire fiscal year?
foAppointed.fpicWhen: You did not have a finance officer or interim finance officer for the entire fiscal year
foAppointed.why: Every local government and public authority must have a finance officer at all times.

foBonded.label: The finance officer or interim finance officer was bonded in an amount required by statute
foBonded.question: Was your finance officer properly bonded?
foBonded.fpicWhen: Your finance officer was not properly bonded
foBonded.why: The finance officer must give a true accounting and faithful performance bond in the statutory amount.
foBonded.help: Required by G.S. 159-29: a bond of at least the greater of $50,000 or 10% of annually budgeted funds, up to $1,000,000.

debt.label: The unit had late debt service payments and/or did not comply with bond covenants
debt.shortLabel: Late debt service or covenant issues
debt.plainLabel: Late debt payments or covenant breaches
debt.question: Were any debt service payments late, or did you not comply with a bond covenant?
debt.fpicWhen: A debt service payment was late, or you did not comply with a bond covenant
debt.why: Debt has payment schedules and covenants. Missing them can have negative financial effects and may point to financial or internal control issues.

auditorOther.label: Any other issues that affect the unit's fiscal health or internal controls
auditorOther.question: Did the auditor raise any other issue with your board?
auditorOther.fpicWhen: The auditor raised another issue affecting fiscal health or internal controls
auditorOther.why: The auditor may report issues that affect fiscal health or internal controls but that were not otherwise required to be disclosed. Your FPIC response should explain them.
auditorOther.help: Issues that were not required in the financial statements and did not rise to a significant deficiency or material weakness.
